_README: The template bank. Shapes, not questions: every slot is filled from a line
the owner confirmed on the fact sheet or from the session's run inputs, so
every generated query is traceable to something a human vouched for.
NO LLM WRITES ENTRIES HERE. docs/query-generation-plan.md §1b forbids
LLM-originated queries — source, draft, format, never originate. Adding a
shape is a human editorial act, and `provenance` records how it was sourced:
verbatim       lifted from a real buyer's words (a review, a support
ticket, a sales call transcript)
near_verbatim  a real phrasing with the brand or place swapped out
constructed    a pure shape nobody said in these words
WHOSE LANGUAGE IS THIS? A LOCAL TRADE'S. Read the problem_aware and
informational shapes: something breaks, somebody comes out, there is a first
visit and a permit. That is the only field this bank was sourced for, and
substituting a different {category} into it does not make it that field's
questions — it produced "my digital marketing agency keeps breaking" for a
B2B agency. Per query-generation-plan.md §0.5.2, brand and comparison are
field-independent and belong to everyone; every other bucket here is
local-trade language awaiting a per-field twin. Do not treat this file as the
default bank for a business that is not a local trade.
EVERY SHAPE MUST CARRY AT LEAST ONE SLOT. A shape with none is the same
string for every client alive: it cannot be traced to a line the owner
confirmed, and no answer to it could mention them. Three used to be here —
"how do I stop this from happening again", "is this an emergency or can it
wait until Monday", "what does it usually cost to fix this myself vs hiring
someone" — each a guaranteed zero in the numerator and a live +1 in the
denominator of a rate a client is quoted. generate.py drops them now, so a
slotless shape added here would silently never be used.
A shape whose slots cannot all be filled is DROPPED, never partially filled:
a literal {city} reaching an engine scores as a loss on a question nobody
asked. Keys are IntentBucket values; both funnels live in one file because
the local fallback and the product path share the brand and comparison banks.
